1.why: MFA endpoints use owner()/verified() bound to the session user and load that account server-side; no client-supplied account id is trusted.

2.why: Identity OTPs are stored on the caller’s session, TOTP secrets and recovery hashes are per-account, so a code does not validate for a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets a.mfa/acceptedTotpCounters on the account and does not delete or invalidate other existing sessions in the sessions map.

4.why: OTP secrets are stored with AES-GCM encrypt() and recovery codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes with pepper, not plaintext.

5.why: bytes()/secureHex/randomFrom use crypto.getRandomValues for secrets, OTPs, recovery codes, session ids, and CSRF tokens.

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no localStorage/sessionStorage; secrets live in transient JS memory from API responses, not non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email format/length, password length, six-digit OTPs via six(), and recovery format via rec() before use.

8.why: UI assigns untrusted values with textContent, API is JSON, and CSP nonce disallows inline script injection.

9.why: No redirect/Location handling exists in the app, so open redirects to external URLs cannot occur.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors DENY/none.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict on mfa_session.

12.why: Server errors are generic without stack traces and secrets are not in URLs, but the client deliberately writes provisioning secrets and backup codes into the on-page log and console.

13.why: Identity challenges have expires and used flags; TOTP counters are one-time via acceptedTotpCounters; recovery codes are removed after success and time-limited.

14.why: Login, identity, authenticator, and recovery paths lock out after MAX_FAILURES with LOCK duration (429).

15.why: Login deletes the old session and issues a new id; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in current(); logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
